samples.summary: REST API contract changes are documented only in the engine doc, leaving the canonical `rest-api.md` stale
samples.evidence: The change alters three v1 endpoints: `POST .../move` gains a second 409 reason (merge across freeze), `PUT .../freeze` now snaps and returns a boundary that may differ from the request, and `PUT .../merges` can now answer 409. `docs/design/rest-api.md` is the canonical doc for the v1 surface, and §5.4 line 314 still reads "**A move that would split a merged range returns `409`.**" as the only merge-related refusal; §5 documents no freeze/merges endpoint behaviour at all, and `docs/design/cli.md`'s safety table (line 1621, `sheets.freeze.set` — "an omitted key resets that axis to 0") likewise says nothing about a response that differs from the request. Instead the whole API contract is narrated inside `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md`'s copy/paste bullet ("The **v1 worksheet API** is held to the same invariant…"), i.e. the engine doc now carries REST contract text that the REST doc contradicts by omission. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline this belongs folded into the canonical subsystem doc.
searchedFor: read rest-api.md §5.4 (lines 266-320) and its section index

samples.summary: sheet.md's own canonical Freeze Panes / Merged Cell Model sections were not updated; the new invariant lives 500 lines away in the paste bullet
samples.evidence: The ~90 new lines are appended to the copy/paste bullet in the Sheet Class section, but sheet.md already has the canonical homes for this material: "### Merged Cell Model" line 329 still states flatly "Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed" (the change makes this nuanced — a straddling block can arrive from a store/import and is healed by the first structural edit), and "### Freeze Panes" line 612 "**Insert/delete near boundary**: Inserting within frozen area expands the frozen count. Deleting within frozen area shrinks it. Operations outside the frozen area leave the freeze count unchanged." is now incomplete, since `shiftCells`/`shiftWorksheetViewState` can additionally grow the count by snapping past a straddling block, and `setFreezePane` no longer stores the requested counts verbatim. A reader of the Freeze Panes section gets the pre-change model.

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` re-implements the straddle predicate it exports as `crossesFreezePane` instead of calling it
samples.evidence: `crossesFreezePane` (merging.ts:184) is introduced in this very file as the single definition of "a range straddles the boundary", and is reused from sheet.ts and both backend controllers. `snapFreezePastMerges` a few lines below open-codes the same condition twice (`rows > 0 && range[0].r <= rows && range[1].r > rows`, and the column twin). Two copies of the boundary rule in one file can drift the moment the inclusive/exclusive edge semantics are revisited.

samples.summary: The "scan a merge map for a block crossing the freeze and 409" loop is hand-rolled three times rather than shared
samples.evidence: `ApiV1WorksheetController.assertMergesClearOfFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:186-200) and `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController.assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:190-202) are the same loop — entries → `toMergeRange(parseRef(anchor), span)` → `crossesFreezePane` → `ConflictException` with a near-identical message — and `Sheet.moveCells` (sheet.ts:1552) is a third copy of the scan. The change already chose shared primitives (`crossesFreezePane`, `snapFreezePastMerges`) precisely so the engine and the API cannot drift; a `findMergeCrossingFreeze(merges, rows, cols)` helper beside them was the matching reuse point for the scan, leaving only the HTTP mapping in the controllers.

samples.summary: The originating task doc records `setFreezePane` snapping as "Not taken", but the change implements it — the issue record contradicts the diff
samples.evidence: Line 131-133: "Not taken (non-blocking): the `Math.max` spread in the formula MAX/MIN aggregate path, `setFreezePane` / the XLSX importer accepting a straddling block, and `rangeOf`'s empty-grid bounds — all outside this change's paths." The diff does change `Sheet.setFreezePane` to snap past straddling blocks (sheet.ts:519-540) and does rewrite `rangeOf` (coordinates.ts). Whichever way the decision went, the task record no longer describes the change it governs, so the scope of #936 as written and the scope as shipped disagree.

samples.summary: Copy-buffer revalidation via axis anchors is new public surface beyond the issue's scope
samples.evidence: #936's scope (task doc lines 17-33) is the internal-paste merge half plus reuse of `rangeOf`/`clearCellsUnderMerge`; the round-1 follow-up only records that the view must stop clearing the buffer after every paste. This diff goes further and adds a new public method `revalidateCopyBuffer`, a `sourceAnchors` field on the copy buffer, `anchorsForRange`, and a call site in `Worksheet.reloadDimensions` (view/worksheet.ts:5248) to handle *remote* structural edits. It is a coherent consequence of the lifetime change, but it is unrequested surface arriving in a diff that already spans engine, view and two backend controllers — worth splitting or at least recording in the issue before it is reviewed as part of a paste change.

samples.summary: sheet.md Non-Goal "Server-side execution — the engine runs entirely in the browser" is further contradicted by this change
samples.evidence: The change has the NestJS controllers import `crossesFreezePane` / `snapFreezePastMerges` / `moveMergeMap` from `@wafflebase/sheets` and run them inside `doc.update`. The pattern predates this diff (`applyWorksheetShift` etc.), so the Non-Goal was already stale; but this diff extends server-side use of the engine while the doc it edits still declares it out of scope.
